en: The Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of Ardhanārīśvara
Cāmuṇḍī and Ambā; Śrīkaṇṭha and Parameśvara Pārvatī; Mahārājñī and Mahādeva; Sadārādhyā and Sadāśiva;
Śivārdhāṅgī and Śivārdhāṅga; Bhairavī and Kālabhairava.
Richly endowed with the form of the three powers, he possesses the form of the three embodiments.
He resides upon the supreme seat of Kāmakoṭi; his refuge is the sacred field of Kāśī.
He is the daughter of Dakṣa (Dākṣāyaṇī) and the enemy of Dakṣa; she is the wielder of the trident (Śūlinī) and he is the bearer of the trident (Śūladhāraka).
She is the parrot within the cage of the syllable *hrīṃ*, possessing the form of Hari and Śaṅkara;
she is the mother of the illustrious Gaṇeśa and the birthplace of the six-faced one (Kārttikeya).
Seated upon the thrones of the five *pretas*, she bears the nature of the five *Brahmans*.

The severer of Caṇḍa’s and Muṇḍa’s heads; the taker of Jalandhara’s head. The one borne by a lion; the one mounted upon a bull. The one with the luster of a blue lotus; the one with the radiance of crystal.
The destroyer of the demon Mahiṣāsura; the crusher of the demon Gajāsura.
Mahābalā, who dwells on Acala; Mahākailāsavāsabhū;
Bhadrī, Kālī, Vīrabhadra, Mīnākṣī, and Sundareśvara;
the destroyer of Bhaṇḍāsura and others; and the crusher of the wicked Andhaka.
The destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha; the leader of Madhurāpura. Rich in the nature of the three periods of time; the ordainer of the three tasks.
Born of the Mountain; the Lord of the Mountain. The Vaiṣṇavī; the beloved of Viṣṇu.
The large-eyed one, Viśvanātha; the one whose arrows are flowers, the arrow of Viṣṇu;
clothed in saffron garments, enveloped in a tiger-skin mantle;
rich in the form of Mūlaprakṛti, possessing the nature of the Supreme Brahman.
Richly adorned with a garland of severed heads, he wears a radiant rosary of rudrākṣa beads.
He holds the mind as his bow made of sugarcane and bears the great Mount Meru as his bow.
With the moon upon his crest and the moon on his head, he is Mahāmāyā and Maheśvara.
Mahākālī and Mahākāla possess divine forms;
[he is] naked, seated happily upon the seat of the *bindu*, and established on the glorious seat of the syllable *Oṃ*.
[She is] smeared with turmeric and saffron; [his] body is dusted with ashes.
He who wanders through the great lotus forest, he who is fond of the great bilva forest;
he who consists of nectar, he who is the serpent, he who is Mātaṅgī, and the Lord of the Crown;
he who is the altar of the Vedas, the steed of the Vedas, the Mistress of the Wheel, and the giver of Viṣṇu’s discus.
Pervading the universe and taking the form of the world, Mṛḍāṇī is the destroyer of death;
her lotus feet are worshipped by Rāma, and she grants boons to the son of Kṛṣṇa.
Ramā and Vāṇī are to be well-served by her, and she is well-served by Viṣṇu and Brahmā.
He whose eyes are the sun, moon, and fire; he whose vision is the triad of splendors.
Born from the sacrificial fire-pit of consciousness; arisen from the Great Linga.
He with the conch-like neck; the dark-throated one; the Lord of the Thunderbolt; worshipped by the wielder of the thunderbolt.
The Lord of the Three Bends, who possesses three thorns, whose protection is ash, and who is the ender of Smara;
the bestower of boons upon Hayagrīva, the giver of boons to Mārkaṇḍeya;
whose residence is the Cintāmaṇi palace, and whose abode is Mount Mandara.
Dwelling on the Vindhya mountains, worshipped by the noble ones of the Vindhya range;
you are Manonmanī in the form of a *liṅga*, the Mother of the World and the Father of the World;
you are Yoganidrā, accessible through yoga, Bhavānī, and the very embodiment of Śiva.
Mounted upon the chariot that is the self of the Śrīcakra, established upon the upholder of the earth (Śiva),
possessing the majesty known through the Śrīvidyā, and taking refuge in the Vedas and Āgamas;
he is endowed with ten heads and possesses twenty-five heads.

Endowed with eighteen arms and adorned with fifty hands, he possesses the forms of the Mothers beginning with Brāhmī; he is the self-manifesting Lord consisting of one hundred and eight plus ten [one hundred and eighteen] aspects:
Sthira, Sthāṇu, Bāla, Sadyojāta, Umā, and Mṛḍa.
Śivā and Śiva, Rudrāṇī and Rudra, as well as Īśvarī and Īśvara;
dwelling in the Kadamba forest, yet longing for the Dāruka grove;
praised by the nine-syllable mantra, and beloved of the five-syllable mantra.
Having worshipped the nine enclosures and performed the worship of the five abodes (pañcāyatana),
[he is] the goddess residing within the six wheels of the body, situated in the center of the internal space (daharākāśa);
she is served by the hosts of Yoginīs and surrounded by the Pramathas, Bhṛgu, and others.
Ugratārā of terrible form, Śarvāṇī who possesses the very body of Śarva,
Nāgaveṇī adorned with serpents, Mantriṇī whose deity is the mantra; Jvalajjihvā with flaming tongue, Jvalannetra with flaming eyes, Daṇḍanāthā whose weapon is the eye.
The one who binds the sons of Pṛthā with the Añjana weapon; the giver of the Pāśupata weapon to Arjuna.
He whose earrings are the king of serpents, shimmering like flowers due to the clanging of his discus.
The upholder of Bāṇa’s daughter as her bridegroom; the bestower of boons upon the Asura Bāṇa.
Clad in the skin of a serpent, wearing a serpent as his sacred thread,
rich in the beauty of fresh loveliness, and possessing a body of youthful vigor;
fond of dance, the very embodiment of dance, he is the Destroyer of Tripura who presides over the three junctions of the day.
She who is well-pleased by the ritual service of the Tantras, the one who establishes the rites of the Tantras and so forth;
she who is the bestower of the nine boons desired by the nine creepers, the birthplace of the noble lineage of the nine heroes;
she whose bowstring is the bee and whose bow is Vāsuki; she who is Bheruṇḍā, worshipped by Bhīma.
The subduer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, the crusher of base epilepsy;
mounted upon a thousand-petaled lotus, worshipped by a thousand lotuses;
the sister of Gaṅgā, the bearer of Gaṅgā, Gaurī, and the three-eyed one.
Known as Śrīśaila and Bhramarāmbā, he is worshipped by Mallikārjuna;
he is the pacifier of the heat of worldly existence and the healer of the disease of saṃsāra;
he dwells in the center of the lunar orb and is the swan in the minds of sages.
Pratyaṅgirā is one whose self is serene; Kāmeśī possesses a form at will.
Svayamprabhā is self-luminous; Kālarātrī is the destroyer of Death. Sadānnapūrṇā is the perpetual bestower of food; Bhikṣāṭī wanders for alms; Vanadurgā is the giver of wealth. ||37||
Richly endowed with the nature of all consciousness, her form is existence, consciousness, and bliss (saccidānanda).
Richly endowed with the form of all auspiciousness, she is the bestower of all welfare.
She is the Queen of the Kings of Kings, the beloved who brings joy to the illustrious Rājarāja.
By constantly reciting and worshipping with devotion this hymn of one hundred and eight names of Ardhanārīśvara, one shall attain universal sovereignty.
Thus ends the *Ardhanārīśvarāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra* from the glorious *Skanda Purāṇa*.
